cards.text: Friend, this book does NOT warm up. I've seen cookie recipes with longer intros than this. Line one: "This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God."
Then it reaches back to words written in Isaiah the prophet. And I'm leaning in, because somebody's getting sent ahead.

cards.question: In those words from Isaiah, a messenger gets sent on ahead. What is the messenger sent to do?
Isaiah's words keep going, with a voice calling out, "Prepare the way for the Lord." True or false: that voice is calling out in a crowded city.

cards.text: And then, right on cue, here he comes. John the Baptist appears in the wilderness, and the man is preaching.

cards.question: Out in the wilderness, what is John the Baptist preaching?

answers.text: A baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins
A new temple for the people of God to build
A tax to rebuild the walls around Jerusalem

cards.text: And people COME, from all of Jerusalem and the countryside of Judea. I can't get a baker across the kitchen for a warm batch, and this man pulls a whole city out into the wilderness!

cards.question: John baptizes the crowds that come out to him in the ___ River.
The people John baptizes in the river are confessing their sins.

cards.text: John's outfit? Camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist. I've got a chef's hat taller than my whole body, and somehow John STILL wins best dressed in the wilderness.

cards.question: And what does John eat out there in the wilderness?

cards.text: Then John tells them who's coming next. Someone after him, and more powerful than he is.

cards.question: John says One more powerful than he is will come after him. How does John compare himself to that One?

answers.text: Not worthy to untie His sandals
Chosen to carry His royal crown
Sent to stand at His right hand

cards.question: John says he baptizes with ___. The One coming after him will baptize with the Holy ___.

cards.text: In those days, Jesus comes from Nazareth in Galilee. And He heads straight for the Jordan, where John is.

cards.question: Jesus comes to the Jordan, and John baptizes Him there.

cards.text: As soon as Jesus comes up out of the water, He sees the heavens breaking open. I used to wait YEARS for one little slice of light when that junk drawer opened, and here the heavens just break open!

cards.question: As the heavens break open, Jesus sees the Spirit descending on Him like a ___.

cards.text: Like a dove, and my Minty would NEVER stop talking about that. Then a voice comes from heaven.

cards.question: What does the voice from heaven call Jesus?

cards.text: "You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased." And then at once, no party, not one cookie, the Spirit drives Jesus away.

cards.question: Right after His baptism, the Spirit drives Jesus into the ___.

cards.text: He's out there a long time. And somebody shows up to tempt Him.

cards.question: Out in the wilderness, who is tempting Jesus?
How long is Jesus out in the wilderness being tempted?

cards.text: Forty days, out there with the wild animals. Friend, I can't go forty MINUTES without checking on my oven.

cards.question: Out there in the wilderness, angels minister to Jesus.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "Prepare the way for the Lord.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card spends its sentences on a joke and the quote of verse 1. It never sets up who is writing, who it is for or what is going on.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke "this book does NOT warm up. I've seen cookie recipes with longer intros than this" pokes fun at how Scripture is written.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The joke's logic doesn't land. It never makes clear why a tall chef's hat should lose to camel's hair, or whether the joke is on Papa Dorin or on John's clothes. A stranger would say "huh?", and it risks reading as a joke about John's appearance.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: "He heads straight for the Jordan" adds a manner (straight, direct) that Mark 1:9 doesn't give. The text only says Jesus came from Nazareth and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "I used to wait YEARS for one little slice of light when that junk drawer opened" changes the backstory. In the backstory the drawer opened from time to time, whenever someone dug for scissors or tape, and every opening let the light in.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "No party, not one cookie" right after the Father's words can read as a complaint that God didn't celebrate. That aims the humor at what God did.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the core action. Jesus stays forty days in the wilderness with the wild animals, while Papa Dorin can't stop checking his oven, which is a different action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
